narrative: The model estimated your probability of being a bad credit risk at 34.0%. That does not mean default is certain, but it was above the bank’s approval cutoff, so your application was denied. The decision was driven mainly by your credit history, which was the strongest factor and pushed toward bad risk. Your record showed no credits or all paid; only about 1% of approved applicants had that pattern, while most had existing paid credit or other credit activity, so the model treated your sparse credit record as the main warning sign. Your checking-account status of at least 200 DM/salary was the next most influential factor, and it pushed toward good credit. Your requested nine-month term was the third most influential and also pushed toward good credit, because it is much shorter than the approved average of about 19 months. Those positive signals were not enough to offset the credit-history concern. Next, ask the bank to confirm the cutoff and whether a manual review is possible. Get your credit report, correct any errors, and work on building a documented repayment record. Keep your account balances stable, avoid adding new credit, and ask about a smaller, secured, or guarantor-supported application.
